newsitem.title: UK: BAe expects Airbus to take over its wing unit.
newsitem.headline: BAe expects Airbus to take over its wing unit.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc (BAe) said on Monday it expected Airbus Industrie to take over its wing development and production operations employing some 4,000 people in the west and northwest of England if the European consortium's corporatisation goes ahead.
Airbus announced earlier that its four partners had signed a memorandum of understanding to restructure Airbus into a limited liability company by 1999.

"We expect that the engineering activities at Filton (in Bristol) and wing manufacturing and assembly at Chester will go forward to form part of the new company when it is established," a BAe spokesman told Reuters.

Airbus said its four partners would determine by the end of 1997 what assets from each company should be transferred to the new Single Corporate Entity (SCE), and what value should be placed on the assets.
Airbus said in a statement that whatever the valuations, the division of corporate shareholdings in the new SCE would remain "in line with today's partnership."
But senior industry sources said recently that one-off payments might be used in valuing assets to be transferred to maintain the existing balance of shareholdings.

Under the current Groupement d'Interet Economique cooperative structure Germany's Daimler Aerospace, and French group Aerospatiale each hold 38 percent of Airbus, British Aerospace has 20 percent and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA of Spain four percent.
